svg.title: A commit is a snapshot. A branch is a sticky note.
svg.desc: Blank version of the sketch “A commit is a snapshot. A branch is a sticky note.” with all labels removed, for drawing from memory. On the left, Git's object model: a commit box pointing to a tree pointing to a blob, with the blob's SHA-1 computed by hand from the header and content and matching git rev-parse. On the right, the same starting graph resolved two ways — merge produces a commit M with two parents and rewrites nothing, while rebase replays D and E as new commits D-prime and E-prime and leaves the originals crossed out in red but recoverable through the reflog. A shrinking bar ladder shows git bisect closing 200 commits in eight test runs.
svg.text: A commit is a snapshot. A branch is a sticky note.
draw it from memory, then compare
